I bring the knife down through the cod in firm, ringing strokes.

The Chinese cabbage is cut, and I have grated a mountain of daikon.

“…Good. Now all I have to do is put everything into the stock and light the burner…”

I’ve cut up the cabbage, and the white radish is grated.
“…All right. All I need to do is put these in the soup and put it on the stove…”

もともと簡単に出来る料理だし、オリジナルと言えばいかにだしを美味く作るかだ。
それも巧くいったし、あとは人数分の食器を用意するだけ

Fuji breezes in as casually as if she were only dropping by to say hello.

“Welcome back. It's snowing outside?”

By the time the pot is empty, the snow outside has stopped.

It fell for only two hours in the end, so there can be no more than a faint dusting left in the garden.

The snow stops before the pot is empty.

テーブルを立って台所に向かう。

“Shirou, I put the dishes by the sink.”

I leave the table and head into the kitchen.

I roll my sleeves up and continue washing.

If the cause of failure lies outside me, I have no choice but to accept it. But I refuse to accept a failure whose cause lies within.

When the opponent is my own body, there is no reason I should lose. I cannot bring myself to acknowledge defeat.
